pr.title: Modernize SQL Server Express connectivity and add TLS-backed CI
pr.body:
SQL Server connections currently prefer OLE DB 18 but can silently select SQLOLEDB/SQLNCLI, do not explicitly require encryption, and are absent from installed-server CI. Require Microsoft OLE DB 19 over TCP with explicit encryption and certificate validation, safe connection-value quoting and ADO type compatibility. Propagate the same settings through DBSetup and service connections, expose fixed SQL ports, and reject unsupported provider/security settings with migration diagnostics.

Compatibility: full SQL Server now requires SQL Server 2019+ and the x64 OLE DB 19 driver. The driver’s x86/x64 Visual C++ prerequisites and a trusted SQL TLS certificate must be provisioned before upgrade. The optional driver is not bundled/downloaded by production setup. Installer preflight blocks missing-driver and legacy-provider MSSQL upgrades before file replacement. Mandatory encryption is the default; Strict is available for compatible SQL Server 2022+ installations. A certificate-trust exception is explicit and documented for isolated testing. SQL Server Compact remains separate.

Add a fourth installed-server job for SQL Server 2025 Express, including TLS/auth/schema fixtures, SQL/session regression checks and the existing full regression/management suites. Publishing waits for all four database jobs. The CI fixture also verifies that installer preflight rejects legacy SQL settings without replacing binaries or restarting the mail service.

Validation:
- Native service, DBSetup and regression assembly compile; native build is clean (the regression project retains existing warnings). Inno Setup compiled the installer/preflight.
- Before the fix, reproduced acceptance of an untrusted SQL certificate against the original disposable-VM build. The modernized build rejects it.
- Seven VM installed-server checks passed: untrusted and wrong-hostname rejection, legacy-provider and Optional-encryption rejection, SQL auth/schema creation with delimiter-bearing credentials, Windows auth/schema creation with Strict TLS, and encrypted native sessions after dropping provisioning privileges.
- 153 selected SQL values, native policy, secret/backup and SMTP/IMAP/POP3 regressions passed with zero failures/skips on Express. All 18 live native management assertions passed on the same backend.
- Restored/deleted only the temporary VM checkpoint; verified the original mail service running, disposable SQL/test files absent and both original Ready checkpoints intact. No runtime tests or application previews ran on the development host.
- git diff --check and PowerShell syntax checks passed. Full CI and the CI installer-preflight runtime check are pending.

Update the deployment guide, tracker and agent memory. This is the SQL Express slice of the authorized Phase 1b continuation; stop for maintainer review after this PR and do not begin the next task or merge without confirmation.

+param(
+    [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][pscredential]$AdministratorCredential,
+    [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][string]$FixtureDirectory,
+    [switch]$PolicyProbeOnly,
+    [string]$Installer = ''
+)
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+if ((Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).Model -ne 'Virtual Machine') { throw 'SQL Server tests run only in the disposable VM/CI.' }
+$fixture = Get-Content (Join-Path $FixtureDirectory 'fixture.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
+$service = Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter "Name='hMailServer'"
+if ($service.PathName -notmatch '^"([^"]+)"') { throw 'Expected an installed mail service.' }
+$serviceExe = $matches[1]
+$iniPath = @('C:\ProgramData\ArzoieMail\hMailServer.ini','C:\ProgramData\hMailServer\hMailServer.ini',
+    (Join-Path (Split-Path $matches[1]) 'hMailServer.ini')) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ } | Select-Object -First 1
+if (-not $iniPath) { throw 'Cannot locate the installed configuration.' }
+Add-Type -TypeDefinition 'using System.Runtime.InteropServices; public static class SqlTestIni { [DllImport("kernel32.dll", CharSet=CharSet.Unicode)] public static extern bool WritePrivateProfileString(string section,string key,string value,string path); }'
+$originalIni = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($iniPath)
+$application = New-Object -ComObject 'hMailServer.Application'
+if ($null -eq $application.Authenticate($AdministratorCredential.UserName,$AdministratorCredential.GetNetworkCredential().Password)) { throw 'Cannot authenticate mail-server fixture setup.' }
+function Set-SqlSetting([string]$Key,[string]$Value) {
+    if (-not [SqlTestIni]::WritePrivateProfileString('Database',$Key,$Value,$iniPath)) { throw "Could not write test setting $Key" }
+}
+function Reload-TestSettings {
+    $errorText = $application.Reinitialize()
+    if ($errorText) { throw "Cannot initialize mail service: $errorText" }
+}
+function Assert-ConnectionRefused([string]$Expected,[string]$Label) {
+    $refused = $false
+    try { $application.Database.SetDefaultDatabase(2,$fixture.Server,0,'master','','') }
+    catch { if ($_.Exception.Message -notmatch $Expected) { throw }; $refused=$true }
+    if (-not $refused) { throw "SQL Server regression: $Label was accepted." }
+    "Passed: $Label"
+}
+$completed = $false
+try {
+    $testRoot = "Cert:\LocalMachine\Root\$($fixture.CertificateThumbprint)"
+    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $testRoot) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testRoot -Force }
+    Set-SqlSetting 'Provider' ''
+    Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLEncryption' 'Mandatory'
+    Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLTrustServerCertificate' '0'
+    Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLHostNameInCertificate' ''
+    Reload-TestSettings
+    Assert-ConnectionRefused 'certificate chain|not trusted|SSL Provider' 'untrusted SQL certificate'
+    if ($PolicyProbeOnly) { $completed=$true; return }
+
+    Import-Certificate -FilePath $fixture.CertificateFile -CertStoreLocation 'Cert:\LocalMachine\Root' | Out-Null
+    Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLHostNameInCertificate' 'wrong-name.example.test'
+    Reload-TestSettings
+    Assert-ConnectionRefused 'target principal|name mismatch|SSL Provider' 'SQL certificate hostname mismatch'
+    Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLHostNameInCertificate' ''
+    Set-SqlSetting 'Provider' 'SQLOLEDB'
+    Reload-TestSettings
+    Assert-ConnectionRefused 'legacy|MSOLEDBSQL19' 'legacy SQL provider override'
+    Set-SqlSetting 'Provider' ''
+    Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLEncryption' 'Optional'
+    Reload-TestSettings
+    Assert-ConnectionRefused 'MSSQLEncryption' 'unencrypted SQL connection policy'
+    Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLEncryption' 'Mandatory'
+    Reload-TestSettings
+
+    $admin = New-Object -ComObject ADODB.Connection
+    $admin.Open("Provider=MSOLEDBSQL19;Server=$($fixture.Server);Integrated Security=SSPI;Use Encryption for Data=Mandatory;Trust Server Certificate=False;")
+    try {
+        # Exercise SQL authentication with connection-string delimiter characters. No credentials
+        # are printed. The login exists only in this disposable fixture.
+        $sqlUser = 'arzoie;"login_' + [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N')
+        $sqlPassword = [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N') + ';"!aA1'
+        $login = $sqlUser.Replace(']',']]')
+        $passwordLiteral = $sqlPassword.Replace("'","''")
+        [void]$admin.Execute("CREATE LOGIN [$login] WITH PASSWORD=N'$passwordLiteral', CHECK_POLICY=OFF; ALTER SERVER ROLE dbcreator ADD MEMBER [$login];")
+        $sqlDatabase = 'arzoie_sql_auth_' + [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N')
+        $application.Database.CreateExternalDatabase(2,'tcp:localhost',14330,$sqlDatabase,$sqlUser,$sqlPassword)
+        "Passed: SQL authentication with quoted credential delimiters"
+        # Restore the active internal configuration before testing the Windows-authenticated path.
+        [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($iniPath,$originalIni)
+        Set-SqlSetting 'Provider' ''
+        Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLEncryption' 'Strict'
+        Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLTrustServerCertificate' '0'
+        Reload-TestSettings
+        $databaseName = 'arzoie_mssql_' + [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N')
+        $application.Database.CreateExternalDatabase(2,'tcp:localhost',14330,$databaseName,'','')
+        $application.Database.SetDefaultDatabase(2,'tcp:localhost',14330,$databaseName,'','')
+        Reload-TestSettings
+        if ($application.Database.DatabaseType -ne 2 -or $application.Database.CurrentVersion -ne $application.Database.RequiredVersion) {
+            throw 'The mail service did not initialize the current SQL Server schema.'
+        }
+        "Passed: SQL Express schema creation and Windows authentication with Strict TLS"
+        $mailIdentity = $service.StartName.Replace(']',']]')
+        [void]$admin.Execute("ALTER SERVER ROLE dbcreator DROP MEMBER [$mailIdentity];")
+        # dbcreator is provisioning-only. The running mail service needs just its own database.
+        Set-SqlSetting 'MSSQLEncryption' 'Mandatory'
+        Reload-TestSettings
+        $rows=$admin.Execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN c.encrypt_option='TRUE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS encrypted FROM sys.dm_exec_sessions s JOIN sys.dm_exec_connections c ON s.session_id=c.session_id WHERE s.program_name=N'ArzoieMail'")
+        if ([int]$rows.Fields.Item('total').Value -lt 1 -or [int]$rows.Fields.Item('total').Value -ne [int]$rows.Fields.Item('encrypted').Value) { throw 'Native SQL connections are not encrypted.' }
+        [void][Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::FinalReleaseComObject($rows)
+        'Passed: all native SQL sessions encrypted after dropping provisioning privileges'
+        if ($Installer) {
+            $savedIni = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($iniPath)
+            $savedHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $serviceExe -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
+            $savedPid = (Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter "Name='hMailServer'").ProcessId
+            $preflightLog = Join-Path $FixtureDirectory 'installer-preflight.log'
+            try {
+                # Do not reload this deliberately invalid override into the running service.
+                Set-SqlSetting 'Provider' 'SQLOLEDB'
+                $setup = Start-Process -FilePath $Installer -WindowStyle Hidden -Wait -PassThru `
+                    -ArgumentList '/VERYSILENT','/SUPPRESSMSGBOXES','/NORESTART',"/LOG=`"$preflightLog`""
+                $guardSeen = $false
+                $guardDeadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(45)
+                do {
+                    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $preflightLog) {
+                        $guardSeen = [bool](Select-String -LiteralPath $preflightLog -SimpleMatch 'Provider override' -Quiet)
+                    }
+                    if (-not $guardSeen) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500 }
+                } while (-not $guardSeen -and (Get-Date) -lt $guardDeadline)
+                if (-not $guardSeen) {
+                    throw 'The installer did not block the legacy SQL provider before upgrade.'
+                }
+                if ((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $serviceExe -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $savedHash -or
+                    (Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter "Name='hMailServer'").ProcessId -ne $savedPid) {
+                    throw 'The failed SQL prerequisite check changed binaries or restarted the service.'
+                }
+                'Passed: installer rejects legacy SQL configuration before replacing binaries or stopping the service'
+            } finally { [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($iniPath,$savedIni) }
+        }
+    } finally { $admin.Close(); [void][Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::FinalReleaseComObject($admin) }
+    $env:ARZOIEMAIL_TEST_SQLSERVER=$fixture.Server
+    if ($env:GITHUB_ENV) { "ARZOIEMAIL_TEST_SQLSERVER=$($fixture.Server)" | Add-Content -LiteralPath $env:GITHUB_ENV }
+    $completed=$true
+} finally {
+    if (-not $completed -or $PolicyProbeOnly) {
+        [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($iniPath,$originalIni)
+        [void]$application.Reinitialize()
+    }
+    [void][Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::FinalReleaseComObject($application)
+}

@@ -84,6 +84,22 @@ itself — formats, protocols, database behaviour — are in ROADMAP.md (§4, §
 
 ## Agent sessions
 
+- **Inno's Ready-page handler precedes PrepareToInstall.** Keep service shutdown in
+  PrepareToInstall after prerequisite checks, rather than NextButtonClick(wpReady); otherwise
+  an upgrade can stop a working service and then refuse to install. The VM preflight regression
+  checks both executable hash and running service PID; a rejection alone is insufficient.
+- **ADO connection keywords differ from provider-native keywords.** OLE DB 19 through ADO
+  needs `Trust Server Certificate=True/False` (not yes/no). Use `Data Source` for quoted endpoint
+  values; an unknown `Server` alias can leave quotes in the provider string and fail with error 87.
+  Test actual connections and reject false-positive negative tests caused by unrelated parse errors.
+- **Certificate key wrappers vary between .NET versions.** A legacy CSP key can be returned as
+  RSACng. Resolve its verified unique key filename and check it is a file before granting service
+  access; a missing key name must never turn a key-file ACL operation into a directory grant.
+- **VM database scripts must match the test binary.** The original VM carries schema-5713

+# SQL Server and Express deployment
+
+## Scope and compatibility
+
+The SQL Server modernization work uses **Microsoft OLE DB Driver 19 (x64)** and sets a
+**SQL Server 2019 or newer** engine baseline, including Express. This is separate from the
+built-in SQL Server Compact database. Compact remains unchanged until the planned SQLite migration.
+
+The driver name is `MSOLEDBSQL19`. The service no longer silently selects SQLOLEDB, SQLNCLI
+or OLE DB 18. An old `Provider` override produces a migration error instead of a downgrade.
+Windows ADO remains the native data-access wrapper; it is supported with OLE DB 19 and is not
+the web administration COM API. The replacement panel still uses REST/native management only.
+
+Current implementation/validation status belongs in ROADMAP.md and the latest agent handoff.
+SQL Server 2025 Express is the new VM/CI target. Other qualifying engine versions require
+version-specific validation before claiming a tested deployment combination.
+
+## Install prerequisites and configure TLS
+
+1. Back up the mail database, mail files, configuration and exportable secret key before an
+   upgrade. Test restoring those backups. Upgrade older SQL engines before the mail service.
+2. Install both x86 and x64 Visual C++ redistributable prerequisites and the x64
+   [Microsoft OLE DB Driver 19](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/oledb/download-oledb-driver-for-sql-server).
+   Download signed installers in advance for offline deployment; the ArzoieMail installer does
+   not download or bundle this optional external-database driver. Existing MSSQL upgrades are
+   blocked before file replacement when its driver or Provider migration is missing.
+3. Configure SQL Server's own TLS certificate and full chain, covering the DNS name used by
+   ArzoieMail. Trust its issuing CA on the mail-service machine. This is independent of IIS HTTPS
+   and SMTP/IMAP/POP3 certificates. Do not use a trust bypass as the production default.
+4. Configure the SQL endpoint, enable TCP where required and open only the necessary firewall
+   route. For Express named instances use `HOST\SQLEXPRESS` with port 0, or prefer an explicit
+   fixed TCP endpoint. Named-instance discovery can require SQL Browser; a fixed port avoids that
+   dependency. Do not open SQL Server to the public internet for web-panel access.
+5. Provision a dedicated database identity. Windows authentication uses the actual mail-service
+   identity, not the person running DBSetup. A local virtual service account must have a SQL login
+   on a local SQL instance; remote Windows authentication needs an appropriate domain identity.
+   Give provisioning privileges only while creating the database, then restrict normal operation
+   to its own database. Never run the web application as SQL sysadmin or give it database credentials.
+6. Run DBSetup and test initialization, message delivery, restart and backup/restore in the VM
+   before deploying the same configuration to production.
+
+## Connection settings
+
+These `[Database]` keys apply to the full SQL Server backend:
+
+```ini
+[Database]
+Type=MSSQL
+Provider=MSOLEDBSQL19
+Server=sql.example.test
+Port=1433
+Database=ArzoieMail
+Username=
+MSSQLEncryption=Mandatory
+MSSQLTrustServerCertificate=0
+MSSQLHostNameInCertificate=
+```
+
+- `Provider` may be blank (the same OLE DB 19 default) or `MSOLEDBSQL19`.
+- All SQL Server connections use TCP with TLS, including local connections; shared-memory,
+  named-pipe and LocalDB deployments are outside this supported configuration.
+- `Port=0` preserves the server/instance endpoint; a positive port sets its TCP port. A port may instead
+  be included in `Server`, such as `tcp:sql.example.test,1433`; do not specify it in both places.
+  DBSetup exposes the SQL port field, including the instance/default value 0.
+- Blank `Username` selects Windows integrated authentication. For SQL authentication, use DBSetup
+  so the existing protected database-password storage is used. Do not add plain passwords to docs.
+- `MSSQLEncryption=Mandatory` is the default; unencrypted/Optional connections are rejected.
+  `Strict` is supported for SQL Server 2022 and later with compatible server TLS configuration.
+- `MSSQLTrustServerCertificate=0` is the default and validates the certificate. Value `1` is an
+  explicit exception for isolated testing only: it skips server identity validation while keeping
+  encryption. It is rejected with Strict mode. Invalid values fail rather than weaken security.
+- `MSSQLHostNameInCertificate` optionally supplies an expected certificate name when connecting
+  through a differently named endpoint; use a deliberately provisioned name, not a trust bypass.
+- Change protected INI settings as an administrator and restart/reinitialize the mail service.
+  The same options apply to DBSetup's create/select operations and all service connections.
+
+Connection values are quoted, preserving delimiters in SQL credentials without allowing those
+values to change encryption properties. The adapter explicitly enables ADO data-type compatibility
+and identifies its SQL sessions as `ArzoieMail`. It does not log its connection string.
+
+## Express capacity
+
+Express has edition/version resource limits. Passing functional tests does not establish that it
+can sustain the high-pressure mail or scanning workload. Size and measure database CPU, memory,
+connection/lock contention, metadata growth, backups and queue operations alongside the scan engine.
+Message bodies are stored in the mail data directory; that does not remove database limits.
+Use the [Microsoft edition matrix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/sql-server/editions-and-components-of-sql-server-2025)
+for the selected release; do not assume limits from an older Express version.
+
+## Repeatable tests
+
+`build/provision-mssql-test.ps1 -DisposableEnvironment` installs SQL Server 2025 Express and
+OLE DB 19 only inside an explicitly selected disposable VM/CI environment. It configures a
+fixed test endpoint and a VM-only certificate. It is not a production installer. Microsoft-signed
+payloads are verified, and the selected OLE DB MSI is additionally SHA-256 pinned.
+
+`build/test-mssql-connection.ps1` exercises rejection of an untrusted certificate, wrong hostname,
+legacy provider and Optional encryption; SQL-authenticated schema creation with delimiter-bearing
+credentials; Windows authentication, Strict and Mandatory TLS; and encrypted native sessions.
+Provisioning dbcreator rights are removed after setup. The full regression and management suites
+then run on the installed SQL Server-backed service in CI, in addition to the other database jobs.
+Installer publishing waits for all four database jobs. Runtime tests never run on the development host.
+
+VM certificates, SQL fixture users, logs and installer media remain outside source control. Restore
+the VM checkpoint after testing; CI runners are discarded. A negative-policy probe can be run against
+the old build before deployment to demonstrate the previous behavior.
+
+## Microsoft references
+
+- [Current provider and encryption changes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/oledb/major-version-differences)
+- [ADO compatibility requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/oledb/applications/using-ado-with-oledb-driver-for-sql-server)
+- [Driver installation prerequisites](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/oledb/applications/installing-oledb-driver-for-sql-server)

commit.message:
Modernize SQL Server Express connections and add installed-server CI

Require OLE DB 19 and SQL Server 2019+ over TCP with explicit TLS and certificate validation, quote connection values, propagate security settings through DBSetup/service paths, expose fixed ports and block missing-driver or legacy-provider upgrades. Add SQL Express TLS/authentication fixtures and a fourth regression job gating publication; document migration and shared agent status.

Co-Authored-By: OpenAI Codex <noreply@openai.com>

Keep the mail service running when upgrade prerequisites fail

Move service shutdown from the Ready-page handler into PrepareToInstall after SQL driver/provider checks. The VM regression reproduced premature shutdown before the fix and verified unchanged binaries and service PID afterward. Record PR #33 and validation in shared memory.
